concept: Atlas Charts periodic versus nonperiodic date binning
summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas Charts periodic versus nonperiodic date binning. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: For Month bins, a custom date format can include year only with Periodic disabled. Enabling Periodic removes year from valid formatting choices. Labels cannot include time units finer than the bin size; Charts highlights invalid formats in red. (medium confidence)

University of Malta researchers report generating periodic mean and raw air-quality charts with MongoDB Charts. Their chapter does not document the Periodic toggle, so it cannot independently verify its exact binning semantics. (low confidence)

With Month binning, Periodic pools matching months across years; nonperiodic bins retain year-month identity. The documentation's five-year example produces 12 periodic categories versus 60 nonperiodic categories. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A March 2022 hands-on temperature-monitoring article uses discrete hourly periodic binning to show a typical daily profile, illustrating how recurring-hour summaries differ from a chronological trace. (medium confidence)
Charts forces Periodic on for Day of the Week and off for Year, its largest supported time period. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Periodic specifies grouping, not a mandatory sum. The binning documentation uses mean sales by recurring date-of-month; the line/area reference separately demonstrates count aggregation over periodic date-of-month bins. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Compare Periods requires a binned nonperiodic date category and an aggregation channel. Supported bar/column and discrete line/area charts can show cumulative totals or differences from the preceding chronological point; the first difference is blank. (low confidence)
